issues.issue: Did the RAD reasonably refuse to admit the two newspaper articles as new evidence under s. 110(4)?
issues.applicant_position: The articles answered the RPD's reading of an Amnesty report, so could not reasonably have been expected earlier; read s. 110(4) flexibly.
issues.respondent_position: The articles could have been presented to the RPD; s. 110(4) is narrow and gives the RAD no discretion (Singh FCA).
issues.result_quote: the RAD reasonably found that the proposed new evidence did not meet the criteria set out in subsection 110(4)

issues.issue: Must the RAD weigh Charter s. 7 values when deciding whether to admit new evidence?
issues.applicant_position: The RAD must exercise its s. 110(4) discretion consistently with s. 7 Charter rights, engaged by serious risk to life.
issues.respondent_position: Singh FCA held s. 110(4) leaves no discretion, so Dore does not apply and no Charter values are engaged.
issues.result_quote: I disagree with the Applicant’s submissions about the application of the analysis in Doré, supra to the RAD’s interpretation of subsection 110(4).

issues.issue: Did the RAD reasonably assess the admissible evidence, including the credibility findings?
issues.applicant_position: The RAD did not independently assess the evidence on the date of his conversion to Christianity.
issues.respondent_position: The RAD undertook its own assessment; its cumulative negative credibility findings are defensible on the record.
issues.result_quote: The RAD’s cumulative negative credibility findings fall within a range of possible, acceptable outcomes

issues.issue: Should the two proposed questions be certified?
issues.applicant_position: Certify whether the RAD may consider anticipated RPD concerns and whether s. 110(4) involves Charter-engaging discretion.
issues.respondent_position: Opposes certification; the questions are not dispositive of the appeal and Singh answers them.
issues.result_quote: In my opinion, the questions proposed by the Applicant do not meet the test for certification, and no question will be certified.
